cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) goes back past Moses' bill of divorcement to the beginning, where Elohim (God) *made them male and female*. Genesis gives the next sentence of that beginning: a man leaves his father and mother, cleaves to his wife, and *they shall be one flesh*. Two made one, the wife taken into her husband's house, is the pattern from the start.
cards.member_sentence: Genesis says a man leaves his father and mother, cleaves to his wife, and the two become one flesh.

cards.prose: *Of such is the kingdom of Elohim (God)*, he says over the children brought to him. Matthew has him say it to the disciples who asked who was greatest: *Except ye be converted, and become as little children*, or they will not enter. The kingdom is entered as a child takes a gift, not as a rank climbed to.
cards.member_sentence: Matthew says unless the disciples turn and become as little children they will not enter the kingdom of heaven.

cards.prose: The kingdom belongs to those who come small, and the psalm is a man who has come that way: *my heart is not haughty, nor mine eyes lofty*, and no reaching after *things too high for me*. That is the child Yahusha (Jesus) set before them, one who takes what is given and does not grasp.
cards.member_sentence: The psalmist says his heart is not haughty and he does not reach for things too high for him.

cards.prose: Peter counts what the twelve have left behind: *we have left all, and have followed thee*. Yahusha (Jesus) answers with brethren and sisters and mothers and children, a whole household, and Matthew shows how that household is known: whoever does *the will of my Father which is in heaven* is brother, sister and mother.
cards.member_sentence: Matthew says whoever does the will of my Father in heaven is his brother, sister and mother.

cards.prose: Mark has already said who the family is, and Peter's *we have left all* is the answer at the other end of it. Those sitting round him were told that whoever does *the will of Elohim (God)* is his brother and sister and mother. The hundredfold household of brethren and mothers gathers round that same will.
cards.member_sentence: Mark 3 says whoever does the will of Elohim (God) is his brother, sister and mother, the household named again at the hundredfold.

cards.prose: *Many that are first shall be last; and the last first*, he says, and Matthew's wedding parable closes with its twin: *many are called, but few are chosen*. Both say that the order men reckon among themselves is not the order of the Father's choosing, and that the choosing is his.
cards.member_sentence: Matthew closes the wedding parable with many called and few chosen, the choosing the Father's own.

cards.prose: Matthew sets this saying after the promise that the twelve shall sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel). Mark gives it after the hundredfold with persecutions, and the turning over of first and last stands beside the cost of following.
cards.member_sentence: Matthew closes the answer to Peter with the same saying, first made last and the last first.

cards.prose: Luke sets the same words at a shut door, with Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and all the prophets in the kingdom of Elohim (God) and some thrust out. Those who come from the east and west and north and south sit down beside the fathers, and last and first change places there.
cards.member_sentence: Luke puts the saying beside the fathers in the kingdom and the ones who come from the four directions to sit down.

cards.prose: On the road up to Jerusalem *Yahusha (Jesus) went before them*, the twelve following afraid, and he began to tell them *what things should happen unto him*. Isaiah had drawn the one who walks to it: *brought as a lamb to the slaughter*, and *he openeth not his mouth*.
cards.member_phrase: he is brought as a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before her shearers is dumb
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah says he was oppressed and afflicted yet opened not his mouth, brought as a lamb to the slaughter.

cards.prose: He walks ahead of the afraid twelve toward Jerusalem, and what he is about to tell them is met in the psalm by one who says *I am a worm, and no man*, a reproach *despised of the people*. The one who goes before them is going toward that.
cards.member_sentence: The psalm speaks of one despised of the people, a reproach of men, the road Yahusha (Jesus) walks up to Jerusalem.

cards.prose: The blind man by the road at Jericho will cry out to him as the Son of David, and Jeremiah gives what that name carries: Yahuah (the LORD) *will raise unto David a righteous Branch*, a king who *shall execute judgment and justice in the earth*. A beggar names the Branch before the crowd does.
cards.member_sentence: Jeremiah promises a righteous Branch raised to David who shall reign, prosper and execute judgment and justice in the earth.

cards.prose: The blind man cries to the Son of David, and Nathan's word to David is where the name comes from: *I will set up thy seed after thee*, and *I will establish his kingdom*. The beggar by the road is holding Yahusha (Jesus) to that promise.
cards.member_phrase: I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom
cards.member_sentence: Samuel records the promise to David of a seed from his own body whose kingdom Yahuah (the LORD) will establish.

cards.prose: Isaiah's *rod out of the stem of Jesse* is the same hope in another picture: David's father cut down to a stem and a *Branch* growing out of his roots. When the blind man cries out to the Son of David, he is naming that Branch.
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah promises a rod from the stem of Jesse and a Branch growing out of his roots.

cards.prose: *Thy faith hath made thee whole*, says Yahusha (Jesus), and the man *followed Yahusha (Jesus) in the way*. John gives the shape of it: *My sheep hear my voice*, and *they follow me*. Bartimaeus kept crying when the crowd told him to hush; hearing showed what he was, it did not make him one.
cards.member_sentence: John says his sheep hear his voice, are known by him, and follow him.

cards.prose: Revelation's own verse speaks of names *not written in the book of life*, of the Lamb *slain from the foundation of the world*, which puts that book before the foundation, older than any man's hearing. Bartimaeus cried out and *followed Yahusha (Jesus) in the way*, showing whose he was.
cards.member_phrase: whose names are not written in the book of life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world
cards.member_sentence: Revelation says the book of life belongs to the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world and names are written in it from then.
